text:
Morgan Frost is a pending unrestricted free agent, and Daily Faceoff reports Calgary hopes to re-sign him. His season so far makes that a fair conversation rather than an easy one. He has 14 points in 25 games, six on the power play, after scoring 22 goals last season, and his finishing is about exactly what his chances deserve.

The concern is the trend. Over his last ten games he has five points and only one goal, his own chance quality has dropped to about half of what we'd expect, and he played under nine minutes in Sunday's loss in Ottawa, his lowest of the month. Calgary gets outchanced with him on the ice at five on five (about 46% of expected goals).

There's a case for him in context. Evolving-Hockey had him among the top 75 forwards in wins above replacement last season while playing with some of the league's weakest teammates, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a forward who carries the puck in and creates off the rush. What to watch: his ice time, which tells you how the Flames see him.
headline: Frost's contract year, by the numbers
